text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- 200 women have found employment through projects financed by Kvinnebanken, the women's bank. Kvinnebanken lends money to women who want to start their own companies in rural areas. Since 1992 the bank has lent out eight million crowns.
- Norway's womens handball team lost 23-25 to Denmark in the European Championship final on Sunday.

- Widespread flooding in eastern Norway in 1995 cost 1.6 billion crowns. Insurers Storebrand ASA and Gjensidige ASA say that everyone who had to leave their homes has moved back or are now established in new homes.

- The two largest Norwegian companies offering access to the Internet, Schibsted Nett and Telenor Online, will merge to form Scandinavia Online (SOL) from January 1, 1997. SOL will have nearly 80 percent of the market and 130 employees.

- A report from the Defence Ministry to parliament says that Norway's defence industry may be regulated in the future by the same market competition rules as civilian industry. Currently the defence sector is safeguarded by repurchasing and other forms of protection.
